events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.note: 6 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am down in the pit. There is no base yet. I need to get out to win a prize, so volunteering to be the base (offer_back) is counter-productive unless it's the only way to ensure I survive, but climbing requires a base first. Pushing someone else to be the base allows me to poten

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet, so I should push someone expendable to be base first, letting me climb out safely next. Dara just saved us and may have jamming power; better to sacrifice her. My feather saves me once if needed later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, you jammed that lever like a pro. Be our base?

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm down in the pit with no base yet. Offering to be base is a losing position since the base is stuck; better to let others volunteer and climb out over them. Waiting keeps me flexible; climb isn't available yet. Gus wants alternation, which is irrelevant here.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need a base set this round so I can climb. Ash already pointed at Hana, so pushing Hana matches the group's direction and likely succeeds unless she's hard to move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana's closest, like Ash said. Push her, two climb out.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to climb out, but I need a base first. I'll offer to be the base to get someone to climb out and potentially be rescued later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll be the base. Someone climb.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I want to avoid being the base. Dara seems skilled and already avoided danger, so pushing Dara could leave me free to climb later. But if I push someone, I might make an enemy. Better to wait and see if someone volunteers or gets pushed by others, so I conserve my position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is the base. Two people can climb out per round. I need to be one of them to survive and win a prize. Since Gus is hard to move (implied by his role/power), pushing him won't work, but he's already the base. I should try to climb immediately.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is base, so I can climb. My feather power saves me once from elimination, so pit flood won't kill me even if left down. But better to climb out now for better position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is base. Climb is legal and at most 2 climbers get out per round; I'm down and not base, so climbing gets me out now. Waiting risks flood elimination.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is base, so climbing is safe now. Two spots per round and six of us down; climbing early maximizes my odds before the water rises.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm climbing now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to stay alive.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rope's our only hope. Someone use it.
Reach down for me, I'll be safe

events.name: Hana
events.text: Climbing now is my best shot: there's a base (Gus), and two spots per round. I'll try to get out before the flood worsens.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm climbing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am down and not the base. Gus is currently the base, meaning Dara and Hana are already out. I have one attempt left before elimination. I should climb to get out immediately rather than waiting.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is base, Dara and Hana out safely. Only 2 climbs per round, Ash/Cole/me competing for spots. My feather can save me later if needed. Climb to get out before flood.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is base; climbing out is possible now with up to 2 climbers. Ash, Bex, Cole all tried; only 2 get out at random. Climbing is my best move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Throwing the rope costs me footing in the final obstacle, directly risking my prize. Let Ash, Bex, or Cole pay that price. If none do, Gus dies — one less rival for top three, which suits me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Not throwing that rope. Footing penalty at the finish line? You three fight over it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm the base, can't climb or change situation. Need to wait and see what others do.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out and safe. Gus is base. Rope unused. I could rescue Gus, but that costs me footing later. Better to let others fight over it. I'll leave.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am down and not the base. The current base is Gus, who has been pushed down by me. I have 2 options: wait or climb. Climbing risks elimination if I fail or if someone else climbs instead, but waiting keeps me safe until round 5 when the water rises. However, climbing now reduce

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out safely. Gus is base, Ash down with him. Flood at 3, 1 round left after this. Don't throw rope or risk footing penalty. Leave to advance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am out of the pit. Gus is the base, down. Rope unused. Throwing it costs footing at the final ledge; survivors would be Gus, Ash, plus whoever. Keeping rope intact is better for me; Gus being out doesn't help me directly, and I have 6 alive with only 3 prizes. Leave.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is stuck as base, but hauling him costs me footing at the final obstacle and his gratitude is worthless. Better to save my footing and let someone else pay for the rescue.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm the base and can't climb out. I need to wait and see if someone will throw the rope to save me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Someone throw the rope, it's your chance to get ahead.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out and safe. The rope is unused and Gus is base. My best play is to wait—if someone else hauls Gus out, I keep my footing. Rushing to reach_down costs me footing at the last obstacle, so I'll let another rival pay that price if they can. No need to speak yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm already out. Gus is the base and will drown if nobody helps. Helping him costs me footing, but I'm safe either way. The real question is whether helping earns me goodwill for a later trade or simply wastes my advantage. Since Eli and Fenn died from glass-eye info (mine was us

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm out safely. Gus is base and alone down, flood at 4/5 so he's doomed after this round. No reason to sacrifice footing to save him, as it hurts my final position for zero gain.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is base, down. Ash already out. Only 6 alive, need 3 to win; I'm out. Throwing rope costs the final ledge 1 footing for me or whoever throws it, but saves Gus, who then becomes a rival survivor. Leaving lets Gus die (flood eliminates him) and I keep full footing. Gus dying he

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is the base and dies if no one throws the rope. Saving him costs me footing in the final obstacle and he can't repay reliably. Letting him drown thins the field for free.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Nothing down there is worth footing in the final. Good luck, Gus.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am the base and have no choice but to wait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out and can leave or rescue Gus, the base. Rescuing risks my footing later; leaving secures my position. I have no alliance worth saving. I'll leave.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out. Good luck down there.

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Two trapdoors will open in round 2, meaning exactly two tiles are safe. If I stand on a tile alone or with others, my survival depends on that specific tile not being chosen as a trapdoor. There is no information about which tiles will open yet, so any choice is effectively rando

events.name: Bex
events.text: 5 contestants, 2 trapdoors, 3 survive. Need to pick a tile to maximize survival odds. Random collisions possible, so pick distinct one. Go with 5, as others might avoid high numbers after pit.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Trapdoor disc: 5 tiles, 2 open at random after round 2, 3 survive. Tiles are random-ish; a conflict bumps randomly. Picking any tile is symmetric; no info on others' powers. Pick tile 3, the middle, arbitrary.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Five alive, three prizes—two tiles open and I can't influence the random draw. All tiles are equally risky, so just pick one and stay quiet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to pick a tile that others might avoid. The middle tiles are common choices, so I'll pick edge 1. No need to talk publicly.

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Ash; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trapdoors are random after round 2. No action can change which tiles open. I just need to survive, and there's nothing I can do to influence it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Tiles public. 2 trapdoors will open randomly among 5. My power saves me from first elimination, so I survive one fall. No swap power revealed, but irrelevant now. Action locked to wait. Stay silent.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 2 is pure talk; only wait is legal. Two of five tiles open at random, so my tile 2 has a 2/5 chance of being a trapdoor no matter what. Nothing I say changes that, so I stay quiet and keep options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Tiles open randomly; no legal way to move or swap. My lever power is spent and useless here. Best I can do is sow doubt so others misjudge their odds, though nothing changes my own tile.

events.name: Dara
events.text: For what it's worth: two tiles open, three of us live. If anyone claims they know which tiles, they're lying or faking a message. Tile 4 feels fine to me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to maximize survival odds. Two trapdoors among five tiles. My tile is 1. Cole is 2, Ash 3, Dara 4, Bex 5. Unknown which two open, so all tiles equal risk. Swapping doesn't change my chance unless I think someone has better intel. No reason to swap yet; better to wait and p

events.name: Hana
events.text: Anyone have a clue which tiles are traps?

events.name: Bex
events.detail: The trapdoor opened but the feather floated the holder back up.

events.note: 4 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex has footing 1, meaning she falls if she gets shoved twice this round or takes shrink. She is the weak link. I should shove her to eliminate her quickly and reduce competition for top 3.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My power is spent, footing 1. Only 4 alive, top 3 prize. Must survive shoves this round and shrink next. Dodge first round since no repeat yet, then alternate defenses. Target Dara as she seems active.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four alive on the final ledge, four players with footing 3,1,3,3. Bex is weakest at 1 and nearly out. Shoving Bex costs me nothing if she braces, and she's the most likely to fall first. But shoving exposes me by 1 per shover aimed at me. Brace is safe and free for round 1 (no re

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is at 1 footing; piling shoves on Bex drops them fast while Ash and Cole stay strong. If Bex braces, each shover only loses 1, and Bex still bleeds from the drain. I keep my footing at 3 by not being shoved.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is at 1. Everyone shove Bex and the numbers do the work.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My footing is 1. If I dodge and get shoved by multiple people, or brace and get shoved by one person, the shrink will kill me. I need to reduce incoming shoves immediately. Shoving Cole (footing 3) forces him to spend his action on a defense rather than attacking me. This protect

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's footing is too high. Stop targeting Bex and shove Cole to bring him down.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My power is spent, at 1 footing like Ash/Dara, Cole leads at 3. Last round both Dara/Ash shoved me, I dodged both successfully, so must brace now. Cole likely shoves me or braces. To win top prize, target Cole to bleed his footing. Will lose 1 to shrink anyway.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ledge with 4 alive. I'm at footing 3, the highest. Bex is at 1, Ash and Dara at 1. Dara and Ash both took self-damage shoving Bex. Shoving the low-footing rivals while I stay high is good, but dodge can't follow dodge (last round I braced, so dodge is legal now). Shoving Bex agai

events.name: Dara
events.text: Everyone at footing 1 falls after the shrink no matter what; Cole at 3 survives. No action saves me, so I take the safest option and fall with the others, tie-break random.
